To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) peer and parental influences on marijuana use during the transition to college operate through exposure opportunity and incident initiation; (b) peer influences on marijuana use operate well into young adulthood; (c) parental influences on marijuana exposure operate throughout adolescence, but not during young adulthood; and (d) the effects of parent monitoring and peer use on exposure opportunity and marijuana initiation were independent.

Parental monitoring during the last 12 months of high school and marijuana-using peers during college are independently associated with marijuana exposure opportunity during the first year of college.

(1) Parental monitoring during the last years of high school and the proportion of marijuana-using peers in college are independently associated with exposure opportunity to marijuana during college, and (2) Peer marijuana use is associated with marijuana use initiation, but parental monitoring during the first year of college was not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of parents and peers on marijuana exposure opportunity during the college years.
understanding and predicting marijuana initiation among young adults, a population that has been largely overlooked in marijuana research.
the initiation and maintenance of marijuana use among adolescents and young adults and the role of parents, peers, and contextual factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parental monitoring during the high school years and peer marijuana use during college are associated with college marijuana use.
parental monitoring during high school and peer marijuana use during college independently predicted exposure opportunity, and peer marijuana use predicted initiation.
parental monitoring and marijuana using peer groups are the two most important predictors of exposure opportunity and incident marijuana use in college students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

peer influences on initiation of marijuana use during college are more important than parent influences, but parents can still play a role by monitoring their children’s activities during high school and by talking with their children about the risks of marijuana use.
parental monitoring during high school may be a key protective factor against marijuana use during college.
parental monitoring during the high school years is important for preventing marijuana initiation during college.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parents and peers matter for marijuana initiation, even during college.
parents should be aware of the fact that their children will likely be exposed to marijuana during college and should discuss this with their children before they enter college.
marijuana use initiation in late adolescence is a complex process that requires a multifaceted approach to prevention and intervention.
